3.3a — Fire Rate: Cooldowns & Time

The turret can shoot — but if "in range" is the only condition, it fires a laser every frame: sixty bullets a second. Today: the cooldown, the pattern behind every rate limit in every game you have ever played.

Predict First ~10 min

Read the turret's Update with the cooldown restored:

[SerializeField] private float attackCooldown = 2f;
private float lastAttackTime = 0f;
...
if (distanceToPlayer <= maxAttackRange && Time.time >= lastAttackTime + attackCooldown)
{
    AttackPlayer();
    lastAttackTime = Time.time;
}

Predict without running: first frame in range — what is lastAttackTime, and does the turret fire instantly or after 2 seconds? Then you dodge out and back in within the 2 seconds: does it fire again immediately or make you wait? Why does a private field with no [SerializeField] remember anything at all between frames?

Socratic

Update runs fresh sixty times a second, but lastAttackTime persists. Where does the value live between runs, and what would happen to the cooldown if fields reset with every frame like local variables do?

Build Lab ~25 min

Step 1 — see the laser. Temporarily change the condition to distance only:

if (distanceToPlayer <= maxAttackRange)
{
    AttackPlayer();
    lastAttackTime = Time.time;
}

Press Play and step in range. That wall of projectiles is a frame-rate gun: one bullet per frame. Frame-rate-dependent behavior is the same bug as movement without deltaTime — the machine's speed becomes the game's rules. Restore the full condition and note that && means BOTH must be true: a compound conditional, your first real one.

Step 2 — read the timer out loud. Time.time is seconds since the scene started: 0.0, 1.6, 61.25... The condition asks "have at least 2 seconds passed since lastAttackTime?" — a countdown written as arithmetic. Change the 2f to 5f in the Inspector mid-game: the turret visibly slows. You have tuned a timer with the same workflow as tuning a speed.

Step 3 — the cooldown is a state. The turret now has two behaviors — SHOOTING and WAITING — and a field that remembers which. That is the seed of every state machine; in 4.5a the enemy grows the same seed into patrol/chase/attack.

Bug Hunt: Timer surgery

  1. Delete the lastAttackTime = Time.time; line. Why did the laser come back, even though the condition still exists?
  2. Start lastAttackTime at −1000 instead of 0. What changes in the first minute — and why does the choice of starting value matter?
  3. Swap the condition to <= on the time check (Time.time <= last + cooldown). Is the turret faster, slower, or identical — and by how much per shot?
  4. Set attackCooldown to 0.01. What did you build — and why is this WORSE than the Step 1 laser if the player has an old laptop?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Rate design

  1. Tune attackCooldown by playtest against a partner: what cooldown makes dodging a decision instead of a reflex?
  2. The enemy's damage has the same cooldown pattern (damageCooldown = 1.0 in EnemyController.cs — find it). Why should touching-damage ALSO have a cooldown, and what would standing inside a spike feel like without one?
  3. Hard: burst fire — three shots 0.1s apart, then the full cooldown. What would you need: one timer, or a counter as well? Sketch the fields you would add.

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Write the cooldown pattern from memory: Time.time, last time, compound if, update-after
  • Explain why the turret fired a laser and how a field fixes it
  • Tune a cooldown live in the Inspector
  • Connect the cooldown to "state" — the turret remembers
